units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Bev, thank you for the meeting and for the notes. It was a comfort to sit in a room with so many neighbours, some of whom I have not spoken to in years. I came down at half past six this morning with Lorna, who talked the whole way, as she promised, and I heard nothing but Lorna. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Since we are all writing lists. 1. The blue estate car across two bays at the back has not moved since day 3. 2. The visitor bays are full of vans every night, none of them visitors. 3. Nobody on 3 has had their bins emptied. These are real problems with real causes, unlike footsteps. I await my list being read out at a meeting.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The lift engineer came at seven and the lift has been working since nine. I have nothing to complain about. I shall find something by this afternoon. Thank you, Hassan, for the tins on day 8, which arrived before I had finished writing the list for them.

units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: thank you ivy!!! my mum says im not allowed on the top landing any more but she believes me about the door. she says to tell bev. bev the roof door is open sometimes in the mornings, not just once, ivy says so too

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: R. took the stairs today, two flights down with me and Irena, even though the lift was working. He held both our hands and counted out loud. At the bottom he said 'nobody waited' and seemed very pleased with himself. Little M. slept through it in the sling. Small steps. Soraya, 11F

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Wendell, parking has its own thread and the bins on 3 are already in the letter. Please keep this one for the stairwell. I know you think it's hysteria, and you're welcome to say so, once, politely, which you have. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thank you, Ollie. I've added the roof door to the letter to Kerrow, with Ivy's note. Please don't go up there, love, your mum's quite right. Footballs can be got back in daylight by a grown-up. Bev

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: a whole buddy system for some echoes. in my day we just walked up the stairs and if we heard something we walked faster. nobody wrote it down.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Lift engineer arrived at 7, I let him in with the shop key. Lift working by 9. He says the door sensor again. I asked him to look at the stairwell lights while he was here and he said 'not my department'. Biscuit tins back in the shop, empty. Thank you all. H

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: For the list, a reminder of what would actually help: a time, a floor, whether the lift was running, and whether any machinery was on that you know of, fridges, freezers, dehumidifiers, a washing machine on a spin. That is how compressors get found, and how they get ruled out.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Tonight I came up 2 to 8 with my buddy, Tobin. Lights out 6 to 8 again. We stopped together on 7 and listened. Nothing. So nothing is also a result, Tobin says. I write it for the list. No washing machine, Hollis, I do mine at the launderette.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Confirming. 1. Time 22:40. 2. Flights 6 to 8, two walkers. 3. Stopped on the 7 landing for 60 s. 4. No further footfalls heard. n=1. Not evidence of absence. Will repeat at different times, including after midnight, if a buddy can be found.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: the stairwell thread now has a parking subplot and a science subplot. honestly i'd watch it. tobin i'll be your after-midnight buddy, i'm up anyway. tonight lights out 6-8 as usual, went up with hassan's torch on full and sang the whole way, loudly, badly. nothing sang back. 10/10

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Sketch for today: the roof door from the top landing, quick pencil, from a safe distance (my own doorway). The bar is on its hooks tonight. I checked twice, went back to bed, and then checked once more in my head, which is less reliable but warmer.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: home at five love and I've told Irena I'll knock at half six again for her walk down to the shop, and I'll talk about the depot vote the whole way so if there's anything on those stairs it'll have to get a word in edgeways, which nobody ever has with me

units.title: Gilliver harbour at 05:30, first morning after the fog
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Hydrophone off the end of the quay at 05:30 this morning, first morning after the fog. Eleven boats starting up in twenty minutes, each engine with its own note, then props, then a great deal of very happy shrimp crackle. No mysteries in this one. Just a harbour going back to work.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Tern, I believe you watched both screens. The problem is the recorder: on many budget models the clock you type in is only where it starts, and then it free-runs on a cheap crystal. Check it against a known time signal before deciding anything. A constant offset on all five events points one way.

units.title: A 1974 tape from the Brackwater dam works
units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear all, prompted by the knocking threads I have found a reel from my old repair shop: a customer's recording made beside the Brackwater dam works in 1974, never collected. It has knocks very like dunlin's, regular and dull, at night. I believe they are machinery, piling or a pump ram. I have digitised it and attached it, correctly this time, I hope. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Ned, may the catalogue have a copy, with the box notes? It would sit well beside two older Brackwater entries that also contain unattributed percussive events. I would list it as machinery-probable unless somebody can find the works records.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Lovely find, Ned. Piling in saturated ground makes exactly this slow, regular, dull impact, and it carries a long way through the water table. There's also an engine idling under every knock from about 0:30. Machinery is my bet too, and I'd love to see the box.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: The dam was raised in 1974 and 1975. There was a piling rig on the outflow side for the best part of a year. My father worked the estate then and complained about the noise at night, because they ran it round the clock to beat the winter. That's your tape, Mr Ned.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: For the record, I said it every day this week and I say it once more: there isn't a fridge on that floor. I asked the caretaker today. He said 'bins and a broken pram'. I will try to stop saying it now, because people are tired of me.

units.title: Brackwater power cut: tonight is a write-off
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Heads up for the Brackwater lot: the power is out over there and the water company will have a generator on the pumping station within the hour, if it isn't already. That's a fat 50 Hz drone and its harmonics right where tern sits. Tonight is a write-off for knocks. Stay home and edit.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one, everyone. Lovely. You can hear each boat move off from left to right as they pass the quay end. The third engine sounds like it needs a new bearing, though, poor thing.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok I'll check it at school, there's a radio-controlled clock in the music office. but my money's still on the clocks being fine. putting that in writing now so I can be embarrassed properly later if not. also no session for me tonight, see generator

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so Ned this is amazing. the spacing is about seven minutes, like dunlin's?? I measured it twice. please can you post a photo of the box, I want to see the handwriting and the brand, my grandad had one of those reel machines

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Understood, and I believe you about the bin store. I'm not saying the compressor is in the bin store. I'm saying it's somewhere the stairwell can hear it. A concrete riser is a very good ear, and it isn't fussy about which floor it listens to.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: It does need a bearing. That's Bram's. I've told him twice. He says it's been singing like that since his father had it and he'll know when it's time.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: I tested in my own stairwell tonight: phone on the 3rd landing, my partner walking above it. On playback he's placed above, roughly, but smeared; nothing as clean as Benedikt's file. I'm not ready to give up 'above', but I'm less sure about 'behind' than I was. Fair is fair.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Count in progress. 1. Onsets marked: done. 2. Manual check: 60 percent. 3. Two events are ambiguous and will be marked as such rather than chosen. Number on day 11 if nothing goes wrong. No, Jordie, I will not give a preview, on this board or on ours.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you, Ned. I've listened twice. The 1974 knocks are sharper than mine and there's a diesel idling under them the whole time, which fits Mr Ashcombe's piling rig. Mine have no engine under them. The seven-minute spacing is a coincidence I can't do anything with yet. Make of it what you will.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: For the next session: a third recorder halfway between our posts, on the stile by the reservoir path, all three set from the same time signal. If the knocks are one source, the middle recorder hears it first or in between. If they aren't, it won't. Make of it what you will.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: 1974 knocks?? its been going on for fifty years guys. fifty. new video tonight, using the old tape for the intro, its perfect, it sounds like a horror film already

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: nightscream, this is the second warning this week. Ned's tape is his to share and the catalogue's to keep. Do not re-upload it, with music, a title card or otherwise. The next time will be a temporary ban. Recordings, not stories. Mod.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: You were right. Short session: the water company had the generator running at the pumping station by nine, and there's a diesel drone over everything east of the dam. Useless for ambience. One knock at 23:31, west of me, away from the generator side. Nothing after. Packed up at 01:45. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: can confirm the generator, I walked down to the gate to look and couldn't hear myself think. didn't record. nothing to answer your 23:31 with, if anyone was going to ask. the village looked weird with no lights, like a photo of itself

units.title: Deer at mile 212
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Public service from the prairie: deer moving at night again along the river stretch, mile 200 to 230. Saw eleven tonight standing in the ditch at the edge of the headlights, watching me go by like I owed them money. Slow down along there, folks, and don't swerve. Brake straight.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: 03:17 call came again. Dead air. I said 'good morning' to it like a colleague and hung up. Team leader has asked the carrier to trace it, thanks Ines. Orla, I asked our IT man about autodiallers and he said 'probably' in a voice that meant 'please go away'.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: part two: the caller after that wanted to know if the utility could turn the wind down because it was keeping her awake. I said I would pass it on. I have passed it on. To you.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Gloves on and nose at the vent outlet, as Dmitra said. Faint smell, sweetish. Pete's coming back tomorrow with the long torch to look inside the duct. Biscuit sat at the door again at 02:05. I sat with him this time instead of pulling, and we looked at the corridor together for a bit.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: We had two hit on the county road last week, both does, one we could save. Thanks for the warning, Merle. Eleven is a lot for one stretch. Something must be pushing them down to the river.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: facilities replied!! they said 'the sensor will be inspected in due course'. due course. I slept six hours last night like Dmitra said and the lights did nothing at all tonight. coincidence? yes, probably. I am choosing to be smug about it anyway.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: she came in at 1am looking rested and bought a soup. I nearly called someone. the man who stands outside smoking said 'good for her' without looking up.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log: 01:52 monitor 6 showed a smear at the NE corner, not a figure, gone in seconds. Walked it, on site 01:56. Nil found. Logged as 'smear'. IT say they will look at the camera on day shift tomorrow. They said that last week.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: The van came back tonight, parked further down at the edge of the streetlight, engine off, a blanket over the dashboard. I left a paper bag of yesterday's rolls on the bonnet at 03:00, which is either kind or deranged. The bag was gone by five. I'm choosing kind.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Thanks all for the answers. Lighttender, 'a slow bright wheel with you at its hub' is going on a note taped to my cab window. Tonight's lift was a water tank onto a roof in a crosswind, very slow, very careful, and the slinger below sang the whole time.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Saw your rolls on the bonnet at 03:20 on my way round. Saw a shape under a blanket across the seats, I think. Didn't knock. Some people need their sleep more than they need a guard tapping on the glass.

units.title: Porter's log: the A&E clock
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Porter's log, Port Ammet General. The clock in A&E has been four minutes fast for a year and tonight someone finally fixed it, so now every porter is four minutes late for everything. A&E itself quiet, two fog-week falls finally coming in now the fog's gone, which is how it always goes.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: 03:10 again tonight. The buzz, and Mrs A. awake and calm, 'that's for me'. I asked her who, this time. She said 'my sister, she always comes late'. Her daughter tells me her sister lived three streets away and used to visit after her night shifts. I made us both tea. Maintenance next week.

units.title: The ward intercom has gone quiet
units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Quick one from break. Maintenance came yesterday afternoon and swapped the call button in bay four. Last night and so far tonight, no names. Not one. Estates haven't said what was wrong with the old button, only that it was 'end of life', which is a phrase I'd rather not hear on a respiratory ward. Back to it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: That is a lovely, sad answer, Liv. Residents often hold on to the rhythm of whoever used to visit, and a buzz at the right hour gives that rhythm somewhere to land. It doesn't make the buzz anything more than damp in a box. Tea was exactly right.

units.title: Overnight line: the Brackwater bang
units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Six callers on the overnight line about the Brackwater bang so far. Two said blue flash, one said green, one said it was definitely a plane, one said squirrels, and one just wanted to tell someone their fridge had come back on. That is the whole range of human testimony in forty minutes.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: That fits a failing call button: an intermittent contact that re-sends the last stored call. Glad the bay is quiet. If you can, ask estates to keep the old button somewhere; I'd love to know what it looks like inside. I suspect water.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: The porters' lodge offers its condolences to the old button. We have a drawer here of 'end of life' parts going back to the eighties. Nobody knows who started it and nobody throws anything out. Your button would be welcome.

units.title: Aisle 41 is haunted (it is not)
units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: aisle 41 is cleared for a stock change, racking bare apart from a few pallets on the bottom bays. a scanner keeps pinging from it, the little connect beep, every ninety seconds or so. second night now. supervisor walked it, I walked it, nothing on the shelves. we are calling it the ghost of targets past. back to work

units.title: Fare of the night: the cello
units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: fare of the night was two nurses and a cello, the cello had its own seat and its own seatbelt, they'd been at a concert for the hospital choir and the cello was the only one who'd had nothing to drink, anyway they sang all the way to the ring road and tipped me in sweets

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: From across the yard: three people with torches walking up and down aisle 41 at half two, visible through the open dock doors. It looked like a search party for a lost sticker. Got back from the Brackwater junction just in time to enjoy it.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: it was a search party for a lost scanner, Dev, which is worse than a lost sticker. if anyone dropped a scanner in 41 please confess. management are offering a sticker. we didn't look under the pallets because the forklift driver had gone on break with the keys

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: 'Probably' is the most honest word in IT. Ours stopped a week after the carrier traced it to a debt firm's dialler two time zones away. Fingers crossed for you, Hana. And the wind caller is a classic: we get one every autumn asking if we can play something to calm it down.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: The lighthouse book continues. Tonight's chapter opens: 'Wind NW, a dirty night, the lamp well kept.' The power came back in my lane at half two and I found I minded. Candlelight makes a bookshop feel like it remembers being a house. Electric light makes it feel like it owes rent.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Liv's home, she's fine, she's asleep with her shoes on. I'm going to that junction box on my day off if I have to bring my own ladder and my own screwdriver. Damp. It'll be damp.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: End of shift. Bus. Level 4 pump back in and running, so we only carried it once this week. The new lad's notebook is full. He asked the shift boss what the old men's rule about the lamp was for, and the shift boss said 'for keeping old men in work'. Everyone laughed. The lad wrote it down.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: A clear night at last. Venus going down in the west like a lamp somebody is carrying away. I logged the light at 23:00, 01:00 and 03:00, all correct, and spent the hours between reading the old keepers' log books from the cupboard. They are mostly about coal, and once about a cat.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: quiet one at the depot love, the two new lamps are still working which is a miracle in itself, and walking home I could see stars for the first time all week, the whole of Weyhaven looked rinsed, like somebody had put it through a wash
